name: manual_2d3ced
claim: When chunking Base64-encoded content for a multi-part API write, the chunk size must be a multiple of 3 raw bytes (e.g. 12288 = 4096x3); any other size makes an interior chunk end in Base64 padding, and a standards-conformant decoder treats padding as end-of-stream, silently truncating everything concatenated after it with no error at any step

decisions.notes: 2026-09-12 incident: a text file reached Perpetua Core main as a 79-byte binary payload after an encoded, chunked content-path write. Root cause traced and independently reproduced with real Python: encoding 10000 bytes in 7000-byte chunks (not a multiple of 3) produced padding in the first chunk and silently decoded to exactly 7000 bytes, dropping the rest. The same content chunked at 12288 bytes (a multiple of 3) produced zero mid-stream padding and decoded byte-for-byte correct. Every individual encode/decode/API call reported success in both cases -- the corruption was invisible to per-step checks. Full write-up: oramasys/orama-system PR #357, bin/orama-system/cidf/references/remote-content-integrity-reference-card.md.
